validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, active, binational (FERC- and NEB/CER-jurisdictional) natural gas transmission pipeline -- one of the largest rich-gas mainlines in North America. Confirmed via the Williams Companies' FY2000 SEC Form 10-K405 (FERC certificate granted Sept 17, 1998 for the U.S. portion; National Energy Board of Canada certificate granted Dec 3, 1998 for the Canadian portion; placed in service Dec 1, 2000), corroborated by a 2011 historical retrospective (arlis.org, Office of the Federal Coordinator) and the operator's own current (2026) pembina.com operations page, which describes Alliance as an actively tariffed system today -- proving this is not a stale/phantom entry. CLASSIFICATION as transmission is correct (large-diameter interstate/international mainline with compressor stations, not gathering/distribution). CAPACITY (1,600.00 MMcf/d) is EXACTLY matched by pembina.com ('delivers an average of 1.6 billion standard cubic feet... per day') and Wikipedia's infobox -- no change needed. LENGTH (3,848 km) is EXACTLY matched by the same two sources -- see the SEPARATE spec concern below regarding what this total actually represents (system total including laterals, not mainline alone); the VALUE itself is not disputed. DIAMETER was blank; researched and filled as '36, 42' in (42in/1,067mm for 338km of the Canadian mainline, 36in/914mm for the rest of the system) via pembina.com's own spec sheet. FUELSOURCE ('Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, Williston Basin') is EXACTLY matched by pembina.com and independently corroborated by offshore-technology.com's project profile (which explains the Williston-Basin sourcing via the Tioga Lateral specifically) -- no change needed. STATUS ('operating') and FUEL ('Gas') are both straightforwardly correct and now sourced (see fills).

validity.recommendation: replace Owner1/Owner2 (currently 'Alliance USA' [50%] / 'Alliance Canada' [50%]) with a single Owner1 = 'Pembina Pipeline Corporation' at 100.00%, and clear Owner2/Owner2%
validity.researcher_notes: This confirms the batch brief's hypothesis exactly. 'Alliance USA' and 'Alliance Canada' are NOT real corporate owners -- they appear to be a garbled transcription of the pipeline's two OPERATING legal entities. Wikipedia's own infobox keeps Owner and Operator as clearly separate fields: Operator = 'Alliance Pipeline Limited Partnership ("Alliance Canada")' / 'Alliance Pipeline L.P. ("Alliance USA")' -- i.e. 'Alliance Canada'/'Alliance USA' are informal shorthand labels for the two OPERATOR entities (matches pembina.com's own operator-page language verbatim), not owner names, and nowhere is either one sourced at a 50% ownership share. It looks like a past researcher lifted the Operator shorthand labels into the Owner columns and invented a 50/50 split. The CURRENT owner (confirmed via multiple independent sources) is Pembina Pipeline Corporation at 100% of BOTH the Canadian and U.S. segments, effective April 1, 2024, when Pembina closed its acquisition of Enbridge's remaining ~50% interest in Alliance Pipeline and the associated Aux Sable NGL facility for approximately C$3.1 billion (Pembina had co-owned Alliance with Enbridge since an earlier 2022 transaction; this 2024 deal made Pembina the sole owner of both). Sources: pembina.com's own current operations page (which now lists Alliance among ITS pipeline assets); Wikipedia's infobox ('Owner Alliance Canada: Pembina Pipeline Corporation (100%); Alliance US: Pembina Pipeline Corporation (100%)'); and THREE independent press accounts of the April 2024 closing -- naturalgasintel.com, lexpert.ca (Canadian legal trade press, names counsel on both sides of the deal), and inspectioneering.com -- all reporting the same ~$3.1 billion CAD Pembina-Enbridge Alliance/Aux Sable transaction closing April 1, 2024. (Enbridge's own businesswire.com press release on this deal returned a persistent Akamai HTTP 403 to automated fetches and is not cited, but the three alternate, independently-verified outlets above corroborate the same fact, so this is not a single-source finding.) NOTE the numeric coincidence flagged on the SegmentCost fill: this ~$3.1B acquisition price is unrelated to, but numerically identical to, the original ~$3.1B construction cost from 1999-2000 -- a trap for future researchers.

validity.recommendation: no value change proposed (GEM carries only one row for this whole pipeline, so the system-wide 3,848 km total is still the right LengthKnown figure to keep) -- flagging only that segment_name='Main Line' may misdescribe what the figure measures, since it appears to include gathering laterals, not mainline pipe alone
validity.researcher_notes: Per the batch brief's instruction to check whether this row's length looks like a system total: it does. Pembina's own component breakdown does not sum to the stated 3,848 km system total when only MAINLINE pipe is counted: Canada mainline = 338 km (42in) + 1,221 km (36in) = 1,559 km; U.S. mainline = 887 miles (~1,427 km), or 967 miles (~1,556 km) if the 80-mile/129km Tioga Lateral is folded in. Mainline-only sums to roughly 2,986-3,115 km depending on how the Tioga Lateral is counted -- a gap of roughly 730-860 km versus the stated 3,848 km system total. offshore-technology.com's independent project profile explains most of this gap: it separately describes Canadian GATHERING laterals feeding the mainline (distinct from the 1,559 km Canadian mainline pipe) plus the Tioga Lateral (offshore-technology gives 125 km; pembina.com's 80mi figure is ~129 km) -- i.e., the 3,848 km figure appears to be Alliance's full SYSTEM total (mainline + all laterals/gathering), not a mainline-only 'Main Line' segment figure. Since GEM has only this one row for the entire Alliance system (no separate lateral rows the way some other multi-row pipeline systems in this batch have), the VALUE itself is still correct to keep as the system-wide total -- I am not proposing a LengthKnown change. The concern is narrower: segment_name='Main Line' implies mainline-only, which this figure is not. Not proposing a specific replacement segment_name (hence the empty string in contested) since inventing a new label unilaterally isn't appropriate -- flagging for a human call.

validity.recommendation: add Alberta alongside British Columbia in StartState/Province -- the pipeline's Canadian mainline begins in northeast B.C. but crosses into northwest Alberta essentially at its origin, so Alberta is a co-origin province, not just a mid-route pass-through
validity.researcher_notes: Wikipedia's infobox states 'Start: northeastern British Columbia and northwestern Alberta' -- the sheet's StartState/Province currently names only British Columbia, omitting Alberta as a co-origin province. I attempted to independently confirm this via the Canada Energy Regulator's own official pipeline-profile page (apps.cer-rec.gc.ca/PPS/en/pipeline-profiles/alliance), which states in plain text (content manually confirmed via curl, HTTP 200, full ~107KB page retrieved) 'The Alliance pipeline draws from receipt points in northeast B.C. and northwest Alberta. The pipeline begins in northeast B.C., crosses Alberta north of Edmonton...' -- directly corroborating the Alberta-omission finding. However, that URL could NOT be verified through the required scripts/url_verifier.py tool: it fails with a ConnectionError on every attempt (a TLS/library-fingerprint-level block specific to Python's requests library -- confirmed across 3 different User-Agent strings, all failing identically, while curl succeeds cleanly on the identical URL). Per the standing rule that every proposed reference must pass url_verifier before citation, I am NOT citing the CER URL and am relying on Wikipedia alone as the single citable source for this specific claim -- tier=medium rather than the high confidence two full regulatory/encyclopedic sources would otherwise warrant.
